clue.text: Many a matter pertains to Ms Perkins

parts.note: something that pertains to a person simply is theirs, so this word gives the verb 'is'
Sue Perkins is a British comedian and TV presenter; what pertains to her is Sue's

explanation.surface: A gossip remarks that a lot of business seems to concern a certain Ms Perkins.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pertains to Ms Perkins' as 'is Sue's', Sue Perkins being a well-known British comedian and broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: the many topics or concerns under discussion are each a subject of debate.

clue.text: Being a Dad, having tidied up hearth brought in provisions

indicators.note: the shuffled hearth letters are brought inside the word for provisions

parts.note: provisions are food supplies

indicators.note: tidying rearranges things, so the letters of hearth are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A father, having cleaned the fireplace, carries in the groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidied up' signals rearranging the word hearth, and 'brought in' means placing it inside; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being a parent of children as a male is paternity, a noun naming that condition.

clue.text: Give a stir to their new drink additive

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir someone's fresh drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk or powdered creamer added to tea or coffee to lighten its colour is a common additive to a drink.

clue.text: Prurient and snide, lacking breadth

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for snide

parts.note: snide, spiteful remarks are bitchy
B is the abbreviation for breadth, as in dimensions

explanation.surface: A description of someone both lewd and catty but rather narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having a restless lustful craving, and an itch is figuratively such a desire.

clue.text: Nanny's forged surname and identity

indicators.note: something forged is faked or hammered into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: A childminder is accused of using a false name and identity papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' signals rearranging surname; 'Nanny's' reads as 'Nanny is', the definition plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a woman employed to look after young children in a household.

clue.text: Kick and thrash, not as hard but with difficulty

indicators.note: not says the following letters are excluded from thrash

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
ill means with difficulty, as in 'can ill afford'

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out and flails, less vigorously but with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AS and H from THRASH, leaving THR. 'Kick' looks like part of the struggling scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick is a buzz of excitement or pleasure, as in doing something just for kicks.

clue.text: Jane's taking part in Henley regatta

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman named Jane is competing at the famous rowing event on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Regatta is a famous English rowing event.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's heroine is Jane Eyre, so this is the surname belonging to Jane.

clue.text: Quality beer seller joining AA when drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pub landlord takes the pledge with Alcoholics Anonymous after getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: AA here is Alcoholics Anonymous, which makes a drunk seller joining it an amusing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned British beers, championed by CAMRA, are regarded as traditional quality brews.

clue.text: Cut top off sail with whip

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which is taken here

parts.note: to whip is to lash

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut the top from a sail using a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A slash is a long cut made with a sweeping stroke, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Playing out at front of church, sort of person to be good on keyboards

indicators.note: says the shuffled letters come before the abbreviation for church
playing about with letters rearranges them

parts.note: a type is a sort of person, as in 'not my type'

explanation.surface: An organist playing a voluntary at the front of the church must be good on the keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges OUT to TOU, which goes 'at front of' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To type without looking, using finger memory, is a keyboard skill of a proficient typist.

clue.text: A Parisian that's hot and yearns for divorces?

parts.note: un is the French word for 'a', as a Parisian would say it
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to yearn is to itch, as in itching to go

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman, passionate and longing, seeks a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: unhitching a couple whimsically means divorcing them, since getting hitched is marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is slang for marrying, so undoing the hitch whimsically means separating a married couple.

clue.text: Perfect island settlement

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, as on maps
a deal is a settlement or agreement

explanation.surface: Somewhere described as a flawless island community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' suggests a village but means an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something flawless that cannot be bettered.

clue.text: Running fast though middle section's lacking bounce

indicators.note: the central part of the word for running fast is missing

parts.note: running at top speed is sprinting

explanation.surface: A runner sprinting but lacking spring in the stride through the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three of SPRINTING's nine letters, INT, are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring and bounce are synonyms for elasticity or a lively step.

clue.text: Happy son having energy and lots of fun in factory

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

indicators.note: says the letters go inside the word for factory

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in cotton mill
E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: lots of the word, not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A son is content because work at the factory is lively and fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of fun' is FU, most of FUN; E and FU go 'in' MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for cheerful, describing a face full of grins.

clue.text: Twist around final bud or clusters of flowers will grow on this

definitions.text: clusters of flowers will grow on this

indicators.note: twisting things around rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A gardener's advice on how a twisted bud ends up producing a cluster of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of rose bred to bear its blooms in large clusters, named from Latin for flowering freely.

clue.text: Chef's European food that is starter for Ritz?

parts.note: scoff is slang for food
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the first letter of Ritz is taken

explanation.surface: A chef serves European food as the first course at the Ritz.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Escoffier was the famous French chef who ran the kitchens of the Ritz in Paris and London, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Escoffier was a celebrated French culinary master, the founder of modern haute cuisine.

clue.text: They put off novel narrators with gruesome topics

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement
gruesome suggests something mangled, so these letters are jumbled too

explanation.surface: Storytellers in fiction who dwell on horrible subjects might well put readers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' and 'gruesome' each signal rearranging; NARRATORS and TOPICS together are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: People who delay or defer tasks repeatedly are dilatory postponers.

clue.text: Calms down, catalepsy being treated after finally dropping off

indicators.note: treating something processes or alters it, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of catalepsy drops away

explanation.surface: A patient with catalepsy is treated after nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dropping off' removes Y, the last letter of CATALEPSY; 'being treated' then rearranges CATALEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or appease someone soothes their anger, a present-tense verb like the clue's.

clue.text: A 'new' alternative that's recycled and not at all resounding

indicators.note: recycling reprocesses material, so the letters of the word for alternative are rearranged

parts.note: an alternative is a choice

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a new alternative made from recycled materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's recycled' rearranges CHOICE to ECHOIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a room designed to absorb sound so there are no echoes, as used in acoustic testing.

clue.text: Extra unhealthy dependence on taking Charlie

indicators.note: taking away a letter removes it

parts.note: an addiction is an unhealthy dependence on something
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An extra unhealthy habit of taking cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is also slang for cocaine, which makes the surface read as drug-taking; here it just means C.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra thing is an addition, something added to what was there.

clue.text: Pitched high in area of dartboard

definitions.meaning: a high-pitched voice, especially a boy's, is the top part in music
the narrow inner ring of a dartboard that scores triple

explanation.surface: A shrill sound somewhere on the dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A high singing voice is so named, and the ring scoring three times is likewise named.

clue.text: Insect almost settling on deer's backside

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a bee is an insect
a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: A bug lands on a deer's rump.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind is an informal noun for the buttocks, the part you sit on.

clue.text: Fourth grade letter writer's become profound

parts.note: after A, B and C the fourth grade is D, spelt out as a letter name
a pen is a writer, something you write with

explanation.surface: A student's poor fourth-grade letter has somehow become profound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' is 'writer has'; the letter D is written out as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or grow deeper, as a voice or a mystery can.

clue.text: Uninspiring time before ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A dull wait before a formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Overused and banal, so lacking originality or freshness.

clue.text: Notice gong in traditional house

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A sign announcing a gong in an old-fashioned home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for an honour; the OBE is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun-dried mud brick, and the dwelling built of it, traditional in Mexico and the American Southwest.

clue.text: Make physical contact kicking back of foot. That hurts!

indicators.note: kicking away a letter gets rid of it

parts.note: to touch is to make physical contact

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Kicking with the heel makes painful contact, prompting a cry of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking' removes T, the 'back of' foot, from TOUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden pain, the cry you give when injured.

clue.text: In the distance mark, hard by a river, where crofter lives

parts.note: far means at a distance
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Directions to a distant crofter's home beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter is a smallholder in Scotland, and the dwelling on agricultural land is where such a tenant lives.

clue.text: Topping former partner leads to jail (two to four in Pentonville)

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a cell is a jail room

indicators.note: keeping only letters two to four of the prison's name means dropping its first letter and everything after the fourth

explanation.surface: An ex-partner ends up in a jail cell at Pentonville, a two-to-four-year sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Pentonville is a prison in London; the bracket mimics a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is dated British slang for first-rate or superb.

clue.text: Autonomous island nations almost free of The West

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter goes
free of says those letters are removed

parts.note: the West Indies are a group of Caribbean island nations
taken as written

explanation.surface: Islands that have become independent and free of Western control.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing WEST from WEST INDIES leaves INDIES; 'almost' drops the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is short for independent, used of record labels or films free of major studios.
